title: Reduced fetal movements
summary: Any reported reduction, change, or absence of fetal movements from 24+0 weeks.

openingFields.label: Known risk factors (e.g. SGA, diabetes, cholestasis, previous stillbirth, hypertension)

rfm-01.text: In the last several hours, has she felt the baby move at all?
rfm-01.phoneText: Ask her directly: have you felt the baby move at all today?

answers.label: Some movements, but reduced or different from usual

citation.section: Perinatal mortality reviews — absent fetal movements as a red-flag presentation

rfm-03.text: Has reduced fetal movement been reported before in this pregnancy (i.e. is this a repeat presentation)?
rfm-03.phoneText: Ask: has she contacted you or come in before this pregnancy about reduced movements?

citation.section: Saving Babies' Lives Care Bundle v3, Element 3 — recurrent reduced fetal movements

rfm-04.text: Are there other risk factors present — e.g. small-for-gestational-age or growth concerns, known placental insufficiency, previous stillbirth, maternal diabetes, obstetric cholestasis, hypertensive disease, or reduced movements alongside any bleeding, pain, or reduced fluid?

answers.label: Yes — one or more risk factors

rfm-outcome-red.title: Suspected absent fetal movements
actions: Attend for immediate assessment — handheld Doppler check for fetal heartbeat as the first step.
If fetal heart cannot be confidently identified, arrange urgent ultrasound confirmation of viability without delay.
If fetal heart confirmed, proceed to full assessment per recurrent/risk-factor pathway (CTG plus growth/liquor/Doppler ultrasound) — VERIFY local escalation route.
Escalate to obstetric team immediately regardless of channel.
rfm-outcome-red.phoneScript: Tell her to come in to the unit right away, do not wait — this needs checking now, today, whatever the time. If she has any other symptoms (bleeding, severe pain, feeling generally unwell/collapse), advise her to call 999 instead of driving herself in.
safetyNetting: If she develops severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, or feels unwell/faint on the way in, call 999.
Do not wait until morning or a routine appointment — absent movements need same-time assessment.
documentationPrompts: Fetal heart confirmed by handheld Doppler — yes/no, by whom, at what time.
Onward plan and time of ultrasound/obstetric review.

citations.section: Antenatal care — recommendations on fetal movements (assess without delay if concerned)
Perinatal mortality reviews — absent movements as a red-flag presentation

rfm-outcome-orange-recurrent.title: Recurrent reduced fetal movements
rfm-outcome-orange-recurrent.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone)
actions: Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG (VERIFY minimum duration locally — commonly at least 20 minutes).
Arrange ultrasound for growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Dopplers within 24 hours, regardless of CTG result — recurrent presentation is itself a risk factor.
Full clinical assessment: symphysis-fundal height, BP, urinalysis, review of risk factors.
Discuss with obstetric team given repeat presentation.
rfm-outcome-orange-recurrent.phoneScript: Tell her this needs assessing today — ask her to come to the unit now so we can check the baby's heart rate and arrange a growth scan.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately if movements stop completely, or if bleeding, pain, fever, or feeling unwell develop before the appointment.
documentationPrompts: Number and dates of previous RFM presentations this pregnancy.

citations.section: Saving Babies' Lives Care Bundle v3, Element 3

rfm-outcome-orange-riskfactors.title: Reduced fetal movements with risk factors present
rfm-outcome-orange-riskfactors.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone)
actions: Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG (VERIFY minimum duration locally).
Arrange ultrasound for growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Dopplers within 24 hours given risk factors present.
Full clinical assessment including BP and urinalysis (pre-eclampsia screen) if not already done today.
rfm-outcome-orange-riskfactors.phoneScript: Given her history, tell her this needs checking today — ask her to come to the unit now so we can monitor the baby and arrange further scans.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately if movements stop completely, or if bleeding, pain, headache/visual symptoms, fever, or feeling unwell develop.
documentationPrompts: BP and urinalysis result if performed.

citations.section: Saving Babies' Lives Care Bundle v3, Element 3

rfm-outcome-yellow.title: Reduced fetal movements — first presentation, no additional risk factors
actions: Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG (VERIFY minimum duration locally — commonly at least 20 minutes).

If CTG is normal and no other concerns identified, growth ultrasound is not routinely required for a single first presentation at term with no risk factors — VERIFY local pathway, particularly for gestations under 28 weeks where practice may differ.
Full clinical assessment: symphysis-fundal height, BP, urinalysis.
rfm-outcome-yellow.phoneScript: Ask her to come in today so we can listen to the baby's heartbeat and monitor for a while — this shouldn't wait until a routine appointment.
safetyNetting: Come back in immediately, any time, if movements reduce again, stop, or if bleeding, pain, headache/visual symptoms, or fever develop.
Continue to be aware of the baby's usual pattern of movements going forward.

Saving Babies' Lives Care Bundle v3, Element 3

rfm-outcome-green-early.title: Under 24 weeks — movement pattern not yet established
actions: Reassure that fetal movement patterns vary widely and are often not consistently felt before 24 weeks, especially in a first pregnancy.
If she has never felt any movement by 24 weeks, arrange assessment.
rfm-outcome-green-early.phoneScript: Explain that it's common not to feel a settled pattern of movements this early, particularly in a first pregnancy — but if she ever has ongoing worry, she should always contact us again, no matter how many times.
safetyNetting: Contact the unit again at any time if worried, even if she has called before.
If no movements at all have ever been felt by 24 weeks, arrange assessment.
